traits.bark_colour.note: The bark colour chosen by eye for appearance (see its note), as a screen colour: it stood as appearance.bark [0.38, 0.38, 0.32], which is linear light, so the trunk drew pale grey to white beside photographs of the species (2026-10-23). It stands here in sRGB, as bark colours are picked, and the bark rule (tracheophyta) turns it into linear light.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_max_m.note: Flora of China vol. 7, Persea americana (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): evergreen trees about 10 m tall (cultivated in China); the model estimate (species-facts-2026-10-15, confidence high) gives 20 m for grown trees, the range's top.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Flora of China vol. 7, Persea americana (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): blade 8-20 cm.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: Flora of China vol. 7, Persea americana (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): blade 5-12 cm wide.

traits.petiole_length_m.note: Flora of China vol. 7, Persea americana (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): petiole 2-5 cm.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Flora of China vol. 7, Persea americana (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): blade narrowly elliptic, elliptic, ovate or obovate; Simpson (p. 197) shows it elliptic.

traits.sexual_system.note: Ronse De Craene, Floral Diagrams (2010) p. 77, 78, Persea americana: its flower diagram holds stamens and a carpel together.

traits.inflorescence.note: Flora of China vol. 7, Persea americana (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): cymose panicles 8-14 cm, mostly on the lower part of the shoot; Dendrology (p. 446) and Simpson (p. 197) call them panicles.

traits.inflorescence_length_m.note: Flora of China vol. 7, Persea americana (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): panicles 8-14 cm.

traits.flower_size_m.note: Flora of China vol. 7, Persea americana (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): flowers 5-6 mm.

traits.flower_colour.note: Flora of China vol. 7, Persea americana (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): flowers yellow-greenish. The colour is our reading of the words.

traits.stamens.note: Ronse De Craene, Floral Diagrams (2010) p. 77, 78, Persea americana: nine fertile stamens in three whorls of three, and three staminodes inside them.

traits.fruit_type.note: Idžojtić, Dendrology (2019) p. 446, Persea americana: fruit a berry.

traits.fruit_size_m.note: Flora of China vol. 7, Persea americana (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): fruit large, usually pear-shaped, 8-18 cm.

traits.fruit_colour_ripe.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 197, Persea americana: ripe fruit dark green, pebbled. The colour is our reading of the words.

traits.flowering_months.note: Flora of China vol. 7, Persea americana (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): flowers February-March (in cultivation in southern China).

traits.fruiting_months.note: Flora of China vol. 7, Persea americana (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): fruits August-September (in cultivation in southern China).

generator.params.note: Pacific madrone's crown values, changed by hand: a short trunk forking low into a broad, dense crown, its panicles drawn 11 cm long (Flora of China: 8-14 cm), path_half fitted so it reaches its height. Not fitted to measurements. spur_leaf is the leaf card the angiosperm rule gives leaf_size, 1.5 times the flora's mean blade, so short-shoot leaves are drawn the same size.

allometry.note: 11 m at 30 years in the open, near Flora of China's 'about 10 m'. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: By eye, after Flora of China: grey-green, fissured bark; leathery green leaves, paler below. Its panicles are laid out by hand as eight branches, each about 0.4 of the panicle, of five flowers about 0.13 of a branch, so the flowers are drawn 5-6 mm across (Flora of China: flowers 5-6 mm) in panicles 8-14 cm long.
